Smart weak zone detection MEASURED AREAS

Groups nearby weak signal measurements into approximate spatial clusters. Results follow your selected metric and technology.

Clusters show where weak measurements were recorded, not coverage predictions for places without measurements. Grid connectivity and priority labels are approximate.

Coverage comparison BEFORE / AFTER

Compare the active CSV against a reference CSV, using matched spatial cells and the same signal metric / technology.

No reference CSV loaded. Changes are grid-based averages, not paired drive-test readings. Improvement means stronger signal (or lower latency) on matched cells; sampling differences may affect results.

Network quality score MEASUREMENT-BASED INDEX

Interpret 4G radio quality as a transparent 0–100 index. Only measured RSRP, RSRQ and SINR values are used.

Indicative formula: RSRP (-120 to -80 dBm) 40%, RSRQ (-20 to -7 dB) 30%, SINR (-5 to 25 dB) 30%; capped to 0–100 and reweighted when a metric is missing. Not an official operator QoS score. Cells indicate measured sample groups, not predictions or percentage of geographic coverage.

GPS drive-test replay CSV ROW ORDER

Animate the recorded measurement sequence on the map. An actual route requires the CSV to be exported in acquisition order.

0%
Import a CSV to replay its GPS points.

Sequence follows current metric and technology filters, preserving CSV row order. If rows were not collected sequentially, the connecting lines do not represent a real driven route. Timestamps are shown when available but are not inferred or synthesized.

Custom area analysis DRAW ON MAP

Draw a polygon on the map to analyze recorded samples inside it. No interpolated or unsampled areas are counted.

Click Draw polygon and mark 3+ corners on the map (finish using the floating toolbar), or choose Analyze visible map for a one-click result.

Weak share represents the share of measured points in your polygon that meet the selected metric's weak threshold. It does not estimate the fraction of the territory without signal.

Smart network diagnostics EVIDENCE-BASED

Indicators from your measured RSRP, RSRQ and SINR values. These are possible causes, not confirmed root causes.

Coverage confidence map SAMPLE DENSITY

Confidence means measurement density within sampled grid cells, not guaranteed coverage between measurement locations.

Sampling thresholds: high ≥10 points per cell, moderate 4–9, low 1–3. Unmeasured cells remain unknown.

Project save & restore LOCAL JSON

Save measurements, reference dataset, filters, map view, and drawn polygon into a portable JSON file. No cloud storage.

Project files contain your measurements and potentially sensitive coordinates. Store and share them securely. Nothing is saved automatically.

Report insights ONE REPORT

Your existing 5-page OCP SignalMap Report is preserved. Optionally include a technical evidence appendix using Diagnostics, Confidence Map, CSV Validation and selected area results.

Reports describe your loaded measurements only. Map imagery is not embedded because external tiles may have export/CORS restrictions. The report does not infer coverage outside sampled points.

Network Optimization Planner FIELD WORKFLOW

Organize follow-up actions for detected weak clusters. Notes and statuses are editable, not automatic diagnoses.

Tasks are stored in current page memory and optionally in a downloaded Project JSON. Device save is voluntary; do not use local storage on a shared computer for sensitive coordinates.

Offline Field Mode NO TILE REQUESTS

Switch to a local-only field grid, keeping coordinates, recorded points, heat overlays, analysis and Project JSON available.

The browser must already have loaded Leaflet, CSV parser and PDF tools. A standalone HTML first opened without cached libraries cannot provide a full offline map or PDF; basemap imagery is not bundled. Use the local field grid once loaded online.

06

Model & interpretation

Transparent equations and uncertainty

PL(d) = FSPL(100 m) + 10n·log₁₀(d/100 m) for d ≥ 100 m
Prx,proxy = Ptx + Gpeak − AH/V − 2 dB − PL − offset + bias

Horizontal/vertical attenuation is a simplified sector pattern based on angular distance from azimuth and downtilt. Free-space attenuation is a reference, not a terrain-aware prediction.

Unmodeled: topography, urban clutter, interference, handover, traffic loading, bandwidth, exact reference-signal EPRE, multipath and atmospheric details.

Calibration: reported bias uses only training samples. Holdout MAE uses unseen imported rows; it does not establish performance outside measured locations.

Technical references: ITU-R P.525-5 (free-space attenuation); 3GPP TR 38.901 (antenna patterns, conceptual guidance).

Import your measurements

Choose a CSV file or drop it on the Dataset panel. Files are processed in your browser.

  • Coordinates: latitude and longitude in decimal degrees.
  • Technology: technology, tech or RAT (LTE / 4G, UMTS / 3G, GSM / 2G). Select ALL if no technology column is available.
  • Signal: RSRP, RSRQ, SINR, RSCP or another numeric measurement.

The basemap and mapping libraries require an internet connection. Uploaded measurements are not sent to a server.

Universal CSV import wizard

Select your CSV, map its actual columns, preview the data, then validate it using SignalMap's existing CSV quality gate.

No file chosen

Header names are read locally. Use this wizard for non-standard column names and different CSV delimiters.

CSV validation

    Valid rows will be used for analysis. Rejected rows can be exported as a separate CSV; existing data remains untouched until confirmation.
